terms.gloss: go to see, visit (a person or a place)
evidence: Cic. Fam. 9.23.1: ut et vidērem tē et vīserem
Traupman 110: visit, pay a visit to, vīsō
terms.comment: Of going to see someone, especially to see how a sick person is (Lewis & Short), and of going to see a place. “Go and see” is also vīsum īre, with the supine (Gell. 12.1.2).

evidence: Cic. Att. 12.30.1: quod Lentulum invīsis, valdē grātum
Traupman 97, 105: drop in on; pay s.o. a visit

terms.gloss: visit, go to see (a sick person; often)
evidence: Cic. Fin. 5.94: cum vīsitāsset hominem Carneadēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “rare but classical” in this sense; common in Christian Latin.

terms.gloss: call on someone, pay one’s respects
evidence: Gell. 16.5.9: quī dominum ejus domūs salūtātum vēnerant

phrases.latin: tulī scīlicet molestē, ut dēbuī, sed tamen cōnstituī ad tē venīre, ut et vidērem tē et vīserem et cēnārem etiam; nōn enim arbitror cocum etiam tē arthrīticum habēre
phrases.english: I was sorry, of course, as I ought to be; but all the same I’ve decided to come to you, to see you and visit you, and have dinner too, for I don’t suppose your cook has gout as well
It is very kind of you to look in on little Lentulus

phrases.latin: eāmus … et puerum vīsum et patrī grātulātum
phrases.english: let’s go and see the baby and congratulate the father

phrases.latin: abī, vīse redieritne jam an nōndum domum
phrases.english: go and see whether he has come home yet or not
